4.1 Theorem: Algorithmic Invariance and Zero Mutual Information

Let $D \in \{0, 1\}^N$ represent the complete binary encoding of all physical observational data registered by scientific instruments (astronomical catalogs, satellite geodesy, seismic records, particle detector outputs).

Let $K(D)$ denote the Kolmogorov complexity of $D$, defined as the length of the shortest computer program $p$ running on a universal Turing machine $U$ that outputs $D$:

$$K(D) = \min_{p} \{ l(p) : U(p) = D \}$$

Let $H \in \{H_{\text{theistic}}, H_{\text{ground}}, H_{\text{pure\_land}}\}$ be a metaphysical hypothesis, encoded as a formal program prefix of length $L(H)$.

Because metaphysical doctrines specify that divine agency and subtle pure lands operate either through established natural physical laws or across non-electromagnetically coupled planes, the conditional Kolmogorov complexity of the empirical data given the metaphysical hypothesis is identically equal to the unconditional data complexity:

$$K(D \mid H) = K(D) \pm O(1)$$

The algorithmic mutual information $I(D : H)$ between empirical physical observations and the metaphysical hypothesis is:

$$I(D : H) = K(D) - K(D \mid H) + O(1) \equiv 0.0 \text{ bits}$$

4.2 Minimum Description Length (MDL) and Solomonoff Prior Invariance

In Solomonoff's algorithmic probability theory, the universal prior probability assigned to an explanation is $P(H) = 2^{-L(H)}$. The two-part Minimum Description Length (MDL) objective function is:

$$\text{MDL}(H, D) = L(H) + K(D \mid H)$$

For any empirical scientific theory $T_{\text{phys}}$ (such as General Relativity or the Standard Model of Particle Physics):

$$K(D \mid T_{\text{phys}}) \ll K(D)$$

The physical theory compresses the empirical observations by millions of bits, easily justifying its program length $L(T_{\text{phys}})$.

For a metaphysical hypothesis $H_{\text{meta}}$:

$$\text{MDL}(H_{\text{meta}}, D) = L(H_{\text{meta}}) + K(D) > K(D)$$

Because $K(D \mid H_{\text{meta}}) \equiv K(D)$, the hypothesis provides zero bits of data compression. The net compression gain is strictly negative:

$$\Delta \text{MDL} = -L(H_{\text{meta}}) < 0$$

Furthermore, the posterior ratio in Solomonoff universal induction between the hypothesis and its negation given physical data $D$ is:

$$\frac{P(H_{\text{meta}} \mid D)}{P(\neg H_{\text{meta}} \mid D)} = \frac{P(D \mid H_{\text{meta}})}{P(D \mid \neg H_{\text{meta}})} \times \frac{P(H_{\text{meta}})}{P(\neg H_{\text{meta}})} = 1.0 \times \frac{P(H_{\text{meta}})}{P(\neg H_{\text{meta}})}$$

The Likelihood Ratio is identically $1.0$. The empirical data provides zero update ($\Delta \ln P(H) = 0$). This establishes an exact mathematical proof of why the core metaphysical claims resist empirical testing: They cannot be adjudicated by algorithmic compression of physical observables.
